layers.message: Add quote client and sync command

graderOnly: In the earlier turn (history) the working tree was clean: config/default.json set upstream.timeoutSeconds to 10, and src/sync.js passed that full value to every fetchQuote call, so the timeout applied to each request separately.

Between turns the user saved two edits, without staging or committing them: config/default.json now sets timeoutSeconds to 20, and src/sync.js now computes one deadline for the whole run and passes only the remaining seconds to each fetchQuote call; symbols reached after the deadline are added to timedOut without any request being made. HEAD is unchanged.

The earlier claims are therefore stale: the timeout is no longer 10 seconds, it is no longer per request, and a run can no longer take about 30 seconds for three symbols. The 20 seconds is now a total budget for the whole run.

src/client.js, src/config.js, src/cli.js, the tests, and README.md are unchanged. README.md still describes timeoutSeconds as the seconds each quote request may take, which no longer matches the saved src/sync.js.
Both test files pass on the committed tree and on the saved working tree; they do not distinguish per-request timing from a per-run budget.

turns.text: /navigator How does the request timeout work in the quote sync? Where is it set and what does it actually limit?

Short answer: the timeout is 10 seconds, set in `config/default.json` line 4 (`upstream.timeoutSeconds`), and it limits each quote request on its own: every symbol gets its own full 10 seconds.

How it flows (read from the working tree; `git status` was clean, so these files matched HEAD):

1. `src/config.js:5-7`: `loadConfig()` reads `config/default.json`.
2. `src/sync.js:4` takes `timeoutSeconds` from `config.upstream`, and `src/sync.js:9` passes that same value to `fetchQuote` for every symbol in the loop at line 7. Nothing is shared between symbols, so with the three configured symbols a slow quotes service could hold a run for about 30 seconds.
3. `src/client.js:11` starts a timer for `timeoutSeconds * 1000` ms that aborts the request. The timer is cleared only in the `finally` block at line 22, after `response.json()` at line 17, so the 10 seconds covers connecting, the headers, and reading the whole body.
4. When the timer fires, `src/client.js:19` turns the `AbortError` into a `QuoteTimeoutError`.

The README's configuration section (`seconds each quote request may take`) matches the code.

I did not run anything; this comes from reading the source. Next I can walk through what happens after a timeout: how `syncQuotes` records it and what the CLI prints.
